summary: Wrote rtl/cnt_dp.v with ports clk, rst_n, op[1:0], load_data[W-1:0], count[W-1:0] and parameter W=8, matching arch.yaml. The count register is reset to 0 synchronously with highest priority. The next-state logic is a combinational case on op (hold, +1, -1, load) with a default of hold. Count is driven directly from the flops. Verilator lint and yosys elaboration have NOT been run by me; results are pending the runtime checks.
assumptions: Dynamic power is dominated by the clock pin load of 8 flops plus counter bit toggling; leakage in sky130 is negligible at this size.
Every output bit and every state bit is used, so no unused-signal warnings are expected.
Named port connections are used, so instance port order does not matter.
No switching-activity data (SAIF/VCD) was provided, so no power numbers are claimed.
Op encoding width is a localparam OP_W = 2 per arch.yaml.
Spec out_of_scope lists low-power modes/clock gating and power targets, so recommendations are advisory and need a human decision (G1 review) before adoption.
The 2-bit op width is fixed and does not depend on W, as in arch.yaml.
The KB entries kb-ck-002, kb-fc-002, kb-tk-001 and kb-ck-001 were consulted during the run, but I cannot see their content or whether they affected the outcome.
The flow is sky130_fd_sc_hd, which has ICG cells (sky130_fd_sc_hd__dlclkp) usable for gating, subject to the flow supporting them.
The lint report is the final state of the RTL stage; earlier attempts' reports were not provided.
The module has a 2-bit output, so localparams for op codes are sized with a width parameter OP_W=2 rather than a literal in the port range.
The op encoding follows arch.yaml: 00 hold, 01 up, 10 down, 11 load.
The previous_attempts entries are counts of prior attempts by other agents, and nothing in the inputs says whether they failed.

The requirements REQ-001 to REQ-010 are implemented in cnt_ctrl and cnt_dp. The top only traces REQ-011, REQ-012 and REQ-013 as assigned by arch.yaml, and the wiring supports REQ-001..010 by connecting their inputs.
The reset is synchronous, so a gated clock must be enabled when rst_n=0 (gate enable = ~rst_n | load | enable).
The runtime, not this answer, runs the real checks on the written files.
The top has a parameter W defaulting to 8 (spec width), passed to cnt_dp. The spec interface is fixed at 8 bits, so W stays 8 in the flow.
Typical use is unknown: the fraction of cycles with enable=0 and load=0 (hold) is not specified.
Verilog-2005 subset is used: reg/wire, always @(posedge clk) and always @*, with localparams for the op codes.
Verilog-2005 syntax (always @(*), localparams) is used for open-tool compatibility.
Wrap-around comes from W-bit modulo arithmetic; the +1/-1 constants are built as sized W-bit values using a localparam ONE.
cnt_ctrl has no clk or rst_n because arch.yaml defines it as combinational and stateless. REQ-001 to REQ-003 are handled in cnt_dp, and rst_n priority is applied there.
cnt_ctrl ports are load, enable, up_down, op[1:0]; cnt_dp ports are clk, rst_n, op[1:0], load_data[W-1:0], count[W-1:0], with parameter W, exactly as in arch.yaml.
op encoding follows arch.yaml: 00 hold, 01 up, 10 down, 11 load.
open_issues: A human must decide whether low-power features are wanted given spec out_of_scope and no power target.

Activity data needed: per-net toggle rates (SAIF) from a gate-level or RTL simulation of the real workload, including the enable/load duty cycle and the up/down mix; the random testbench may not represent real use.
Formal equivalence or a power-aware simulation would be needed to show function is unchanged.

If gating is adopted, the RTL owner must make the change, verification must re-run in full (reset REQ-001/003, hold REQ-009, REQ-012), and STA/CTS must handle the ICG enable timing path and clock-gating checks.
Lint and yosys results are not yet known; I will fix any warnings the runtime reports.
Lint and yosys results are pending from the runtime.
Need the typical hold-cycle fraction from the customer; clock gating only pays off if it is high.
No timing, cost or tool-run data was provided, so 'what slowed us down' cannot be quantified.
Prior attempt history (what failed, if anything) is not in my inputs, so a fixed failure may exist that I cannot document. A human or the Ada agents should supply logs if a lesson is warranted.
REQ-010 reset priority is not visible in cnt_ctrl, since reset is not in its port list. It relies on cnt_dp giving reset the highest priority.
REQ-011 (timing) and REQ-013 (simulation, DRC and LVS) are verified in later stages, not by RTL.
Spec marks load, up_down, overflow, underflow and priority as DEFAULT needing G1 review; the RTL follows those defaults.

messages.summary: The lint report shows verilator_lint and yosys_elab both PASS, with 0 blocking issues, no structural or port findings, and no waivers. No failure is visible in the provided input, so no lessons are written. The retrospective notes that previous attempts exist (Ada: 1, Ada-C: 1, Ada-I: 1) but that their content and outcomes were not provided.

Recommendations only; no RTL changed and no tools run. The design is very small (about 70 cells, 8 flops, 100 MHz), and low-power modes and clock gating are listed as out of scope in spec.yaml. Candidates: (1) integrated clock gating on hold cycles (op==HOLD and rst_n=1), whose benefit depends on the enable duty cycle and is probably marginal at 8 flops given ICG area and clock-tree/CTS/STA complexity; (2) operand isolation of the +1/-1 adders, which is low value because the synthesizer likely shares or flattens the logic and the isolation cells add power; (3) a single shared incrementer/decrementer (add of +1 or -1) as an area/glitch optimization that needs RTL owner agreement. Recommended default: do not apply any of these now. Quantification needs activity data (SAIF/VCD) from the 100000-cycle random testbench and from representative workloads. Savings are not quantified because no activity data exists.

Wrote rtl/cnt_ctrl.v with ports load, enable, up_down and op[1:0] exactly as arch.yaml defines them. Priority is load > enable, and the default is hold. Every REQ in the module's implements list is traced. I could not run verilator or yosys in this task, so no check is claimed as passed.

Wrote rtl/counter8.v, a structural top with spec ports (clk, rst_n, enable, load, up_down, load_data[7:0], count[7:0]). It has one internal 2-bit wire op from cnt_ctrl to cnt_dp, and count is driven directly by cnt_dp. It contains no logic of its own, so there is no input-to-count combinational path in this file. Lint and yosys have not been run by me; the runtime must run them. cnt_ctrl and cnt_dp are owned by other engineers, so the lint and elaboration results depend on their files existing with matching ports.

self_assessment.reason: The design is simple and follows the coding standard, but no tool has been run yet, so lint cleanliness (for example width warnings on the +1/-1 arithmetic) is unconfirmed.
